about.title: Suisun City Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Suisun City's mix of retail centers along Highway 12, older apartment buildings, and the popular waterfront district creates plenty of places where a wet floor, broken step, or poorly lit stairwell can cause a serious fall. With a population near 29,763, many residents pass through the same grocery stores, marina walkways, and parking lots day after day — and property owners here have a legal duty to address hazards they know about or should have discovered. If you were hurt because a hazard was left unaddressed, an independent attorney can help you gather the evidence needed to show the property owner was on notice. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply make the introduction so someone with the right experience can review your fall and explain your options, all on a contingency basis so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Fast Action Matters in a Premises Case

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Your Deadline May Be Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a premises liability claim, but if a government-owned property is involved, that window shrinks significantly. Knowing which clock applies to your situation matters early on.

items.question: I fell at a Highway 12 shopping center in Suisun City — do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on whether the hazard that caused your fall was something the property owner knew about or should have discovered through reasonable inspection. An independent attorney can look at the specifics, including any prior complaints about that spot, and let you know how California's notice requirement applies. There's no cost to have your situation reviewed.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the fall. Your potential recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is something an attorney can help evaluate honestly.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a slip and fall claim in Suisun City?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall under California law. If the property involved is owned by a city, county, or other government entity, that deadline can be much shorter and requires special notice procedures. It's best to have a case reviewed sooner rather than later.
